title: Career Fails
text:
Most CVs show only what worked. For every fellowship, paper or job listed on mine, most applications quietly didn’t, and those rarely appear anywhere. This page lists them.
The idea comes from Melanie Stefan, who suggested in Nature that scientists keep a “CV of failures” (Stefan, 2010). I share mine because rejection is a routine part of research, and seeing it written down may help anyone, especially students and early-career researchers, who wonders whether it happens to everyone. It does.

title: Shawn Lee
text:
I am an environmental epidemiologist at the Air Pollution Epidemiology Team, Environmental Research Group, Imperial College London. My work combines air pollution epidemiology, health impact assessment and economic modelling to give policymakers evidence they can act on.
I estimate the health and economic burden of air pollution, particularly NO₂ and PM2.5, and evaluate the benefits of policies that reduce exposure. Methodologically, I work with concentration–response functions, lifetable models and economic valuation (VOLY/QALY), and I lead evidence synthesis through systematic review and meta-analysis.
I care about translating technical results into clear, policy-facing outputs, and my work has been covered in the media.
